table.name: text/btl/battle_effect
table.purpose: Battle-end box messages: command learned, item dropped, injury, technique learned, MP bonus

schema.records: one block per top-level YAML key, in file order

block.block: block name (YAML top-level key); the generated header defines <block>_TEXT (and <block>_STRINGS for entries)
block.line: line of the block in the YAML file
block.kind: 'strings': named C strings; 'entries': C array of strings (index = original array index); 'text': the block itself is one string
block.options: generator options as written: storage (named / literal / embedded per release), macro (embedding macro), lines (strings per entry per release), empty (symbol of the empty string)
block.c: C side: array symbol (entries), generated macros, where the owning C file places them
block.used_by: references to the block's array symbol (entries blocks)

string.id: C symbol / string id (first name if the entry has one name per line); null for an unnamed entry
string.index: entries only: array index used by the code (e.g. MOVE_NAMES[move id])
string.null_entry: entries only: true for a NULL pointer entry
string.text: value used by each language's main release (ja: jp_rev1, en_us: us, en_eu: eu); null = the string does not exist there; cut at the first NUL like a C string; lines of a multi-line entry joined with \n
string.variants: every language key exactly as written (lossless); null = NULL; a missing key = not written (en_eu falls back to en_us)
string.release_text: only releases whose text differs from their language's main release (e.g. ja@jp_trial)
string.lines: multi-line entries (lines option): the line strings per language, padded with '' like the C array
string.line_ids: one C name per line when the entry is split in several lines
string.named: releases where an otherwise literal entry is a named string (generator option)
string.same_as: unnamed entries: per language, the earlier named entry with the same text (the generator points both to one string)
string.symbol: US RAM symbol (config/us/symbols*.txt) when the string is a named symbol
string.used_by: code references: file, line, binary, enclosing function / data / macro, releases that compile the line
string.c_definitions: references that are the string's own C definition (`char X[] = "...";` under #if VERSION_...)
string.c_text: releases whose text comes from that C definition because the YAML has none: {release: {text, at}}; already included in text / release_text

godot.access: GameData.text(id, language) for named strings; GameData.text_entry("btl/battle_effect", block, index) for entries arrays
godot.notes: Text is kept as written: control codes (#C1/#R/#W in en_us, {C1}-style in en_eu, bare C/R/W in ja) and button / full-width glyphs are for the Godot text renderer to interpret (specs/text.md).
